root_causes.description: The recommendation service is burning ~2.3-3.6 CPU cores during the incident window, roughly 30-100x higher than every peer service in the namespace (<0.1 cores), while error rate, latency, memory and restarts all remain normal. This isolated compute saturation is the injected fault and matches the incident id recommendation-cpu_stress-seed42.

evidence.observed_value: mean=2.343 cores, p95=3.604, max=3.608 during window
evidence.expected_baseline: peer services <0.1 cores (checkout 0.003, frontend 0.070, product-catalog 0.025, cart 0.007, payment 0.008)
error_rate < 0.01 — confirms no request failures, isolating fault to CPU compute

root_causes.description: Secondary consideration: if the CPU contention caused throttling, recommendation p99 latency could be degraded. However, measured p99 (~19-24 ms) shows no convincing anomaly versus baseline, so this is a weak alternative rather than the primary root cause.

evidence.expected_baseline: p99 ~24 ms; no significant latency spike observed

root_causes.description: Tertiary consideration: recommendation memory working set is stable at ~106 MB with no growth, so memory stress is effectively ruled out; retained only as a low-confidence alternate.

evidence.observed_value: mean=105861666 bytes (~106 MB), max=108965888 bytes, stable

remediation_steps: Confirm CPU saturation on recommendation pods by inspecting per-pod CPU usage and throttling metrics.
Identify and remove the CPU-stress workload/hog injected into the recommendation service (e.g. stress-ng sidecar or runaway compute loop).
Apply/raise CPU limits and requests for the recommendation deployment and enable CPU-throttling alerts.
Horizontally scale the recommendation deployment if the load is legitimate, then verify CPU returns to ~0.02-0.1 cores baseline.
Verify frontend→recommendation call latency/throughput recovers after CPU normalizes.
